meta.output:
# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)


# Examples

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
  
  return ageNextYear
}

const userObjectsList = []

const usersName = "Frank"
const usersAge = 32

const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})

userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})


```

Done. The screenshot (`assets/image.png`) was unavailable, so I proceeded from source — the human feedback ("no way to edit this in the UI") is addressed by the pipeline base-branch editor in Project Settings → Named Workflows, which this branch deep-links to from the board, task detail, and task-creation surfaces.

**What I found and fixed**

The previous CI failure (`Unit Tests (frontend)`, 6 failures in `ProjectSettings.test.jsx`) was a real regression introduced by this branch's deep-link work in `frontend/src/components/settings/ProjectSettings.jsx`. The URL-follow effect treated a *constant* "no section in the URL" as "switch to the project tab". In any render outside a `/settings/:section` route (exactly how the unit tests render the component — `MemoryRouter` with no `Routes`, so `useParams()` never yields `section`), every tab click was immediately reverted, so the Aliases tab never rendered. The fix: the effect now reacts only to *changes* of the URL-named section (tracked in a `lastUrlSectionRef`), not to a static URL. Mount-time deep links, same-view URL navigation, guard-blocked URL rewrites, and the bare-`/settings` reset all still work — the 10 deep-link tests confirm this.

**Feature state (per-pipeline base branch)** — verified wired end-to-end: `normalizeBaseBranchUpdate`/`normalizeWorkflow` persist and validate `baseBranch` (absent = untouched, blank/null = clear to repo default, invalid = loud 400, never silent fallback); `resolveTaskBaseBranch` resolves task-pinned → pipeline-live → repo default; task branches are created off, synced to, and merged back into the resolved base (`taskBranches.js`, `commandStages.js`); the task pins `baseBranch` in frontmatter; the UI editor lives in `WorkflowManagementPanel.jsx` with create/update plumbing through `useWorkflow.js`; the runner's `checkoutPrimaryBase` adopts a backend-pushed base from `origin/<base>` (never forks, never moves an existing local branch) so remote runners don't fail a prepared stage.

**Verification (all run locally, all green)**
- Frontend unit tests: 4929 passed, 0 failed (was 6 failed in CI) — includes the 10 deep-link tests and 72 ProjectSettings tests that pin the fixed behaviour
- API unit tests: 461 files, 7582 passed / 1 skipped
- Runner tests (`node --test`, full gate file list incl. `ciBranchWorkdir.test.js`): pass
- `lint:frontend`: 0 errors; jsdoc-`@example` check, settings-duplicate check, proof-hygiene, binary-guard, one-function-per-file: all pass
- `build:frontend`: succeeds

No functionality regressed — the only behavioural change is the tab-click fix; the change is one focused hunk in `ProjectSettings.jsx:124-131` with the rationale documented in the comment block per the KB code standards.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: capture-screenshot.mjs
 * @description Standalone headless Playwright utility for capturing deterministic
 * screenshots during PR review or verification stages without running ad-hoc background servers.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/<task-id>"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --url "http://localhost:3100/#/orchestrator" --out "./docs/tasks/task-1/screenshot.png"
 *   node scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs --path "#/tasks/9940bbbc" --out "./docs/tasks/9940bbbc/stage-review.png"
 *
 * Output default (no --out): resolves the current task id — $TASK_ID, else
 *   $KAINBAIN_TASK_ID, else the kb/<task-id> branch name — and writes to
 *   docs/tasks/<task-id>/screenshot-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.png (directory created).
 *   An explicit --out always wins. With no discoverable id the script exits
 *   non-zero naming the expected --out form instead of writing to repo root.
 *   A default name already taken by an earlier same-second capture gains a
 *   -01, -02, ... suffix instead of overwriting (explicit --out keeps
 *   today's exact overwrite behavior). A flag token right after --out
 *   counts as a missing value, never as a path.
 *
 * Fails fast (exit 1, before launching a browser) when no task id is
 *   discoverable, when the id is unsafe for a path, or when all 99
 *   same-second fallback names are taken — each message shows the --out
 *   form to pass instead.
 *
 * Proof checklist (canonical rules: docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md):
 *   1. This script writes bytes directly — never open the PNG in an editor
 *      or rewrite it with a text-oriented tool (UTF-8 round-trips corrupt
 *      it: magic `ef bf bd` instead of `89 50 4e 47`).
 *   2. Before claiming validity: `xxd -l 8 <out>` (expect `8950 4e47…`)
 *      and `file <out>` (expect `PNG image data`, not `data`).
 *   3. This script self-verifies PNG magic right after writing and fails
 *      fast when the write was interrupted — quote its `PNG magic
 *      verified` line as the validity evidence, then run the pre-handoff
 *      gate `npm run check:binaries` (CI re-verifies every proof image
 *      via `npm run check:proof-hygiene`).
 ***/

import path from "node:path";
import fs from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

/***
 * MARK: verifyPngMagic
 * @description Verifies a capture wrote intact PNG bytes by comparing the
 *   file's leading head against the PNG magic `89504e47`. Non-PNG outputs
 *   are skipped, never failed; a missing or empty capture FAILS, so a
 *   screenshot that never landed can never be claimed valid.
 * @example verifyPngMagic("/repo/docs/tasks/x/shot-proof.png") => { ok: true, ... }
 * @param {string} absPath - Absolute path of the capture output.
 * @returns {{ ok: boolean, expected: string|null, actual: string|null, skipped?: string, error?: string }}
 ***/
export function verifyPngMagic(absPath) {
	const fileExtension = path.extname(absPath).toLowerCase();
	if (fileExtension !== ".png") {
		return { ok: true, expected: null, actual: null, skipped: `not a PNG output (${fileExtension || "(none)"})` };
	}
	const expected = "89504e47";

## Per-Pipeline Base Branch

Each named workflow (pipeline) can name its own **base branch** — the branch
that pipeline treats as its main branch. Set it in the pipeline settings
(Project Settings → Named Workflows tab, `#/settings/workflows`; `Base
branch` field, blank = repo default) — the board's pipeline menu (Manage
Workflows), the task detail page, the inline add-task form, and the
create-task dialog all link there from the base branch they display, and
settings search finds it under "base branch" — or via
`POST/PATCH /projects/:id/workflows…` (`baseBranch`, stored in
`.kainbain/project.json`). Every "default branch" step in this document then
means the task's **effective base branch**: task branches are created off it,
the merge stage merges back into it (and pushes it), post-stage finalise
returns to it, CI `runOnBranch: "primary"` runs on it, and review/diff views
compare the task branch against it.

Resolution order per task: the task's pinned snapshot → the pipeline's live
setting → the repo default. The snapshot is pinned at task creation (pure
data, no git — the serialization gate below still holds), so re-pointing a
pipeline only affects subsequently created tasks; in-flight tasks keep
merging into the base they started with. One caveat when adopting
this on a live install: tasks created before this feature have no snapshot,
so they follow the pipeline's live setting — set the base before those tasks
merge if you want them on the feature branch too. A configured base that
does not exist yet is auto-created from the repo default tip (adopting
`origin/<base>` when the remote already has it) and pushed best-effort, so a
fresh feature branch just works. Remote runners adopt a pushed base the same
way before `primary` CI runs (fetch, then track `origin/<base>` when the
local branch is missing — never forked, never moved when it already exists),
so a stage the backend prepared never fails for a branch the runner simply
never fetched. An invalid git name refuses loudly (400 at the API, inline
error in the UI) and is never silently replaced with `main`.

One deliberate exception: the KainBain self-deploy continuity path
===SURVEY answers===
  "answers": {
    "q1": {
      "selected": [
        "On each pipeline — one setting per pipeline that applies to all of its tasks"

title: Materialize task-referenced image assets into the runner workspace
status: completed | stage: stage-1794594754686
--- goal ---
PROBLEM: Tasks often reference screenshots as ![image.png](assets/image.png), but the referenced file is absent from the runner workspace, so agents must guess at the visual defect from source alone, wasting effort and risking a wrong fix. FIX: When a task description references assets/* (or any attached file), the engine/runner must either (a) copy the attachment into the workspace at the referenced relative path before the first stage runs, or (b) if the attachment is genuinely missing, replace the dead reference in the rendered prompt with an explicit MISSING-ASSET warning naming the file, so agents fail fast instead of silently planning around a phantom screenshot. Acceptance: a task referencing assets/image.png either has a readable file at that path in the workspace or its prompt carries the missing-asset warning. title: Default screenshot capture output to the task docs folder
status: completed | stage: stage-1794594754686
--- goal ---
# Default screenshot capture output to the task docs folder

## Problem
The repo's screenshot tool (`scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs`) writes PNG bytes directly, which is the binary-safe way for agents to attach proof screenshots. But its `--out` flag defaults to `screenshot.png` in the repo root (code: `getArg("--out") || "screenshot.png"`). Every agent must therefore remember to pass an explicit `--out docs/tasks/<task-id>/<name>-proof.png` on every capture. If an agent forgets or improvises, the PNG lands at the repo root, trips the repo-root scratch-hygiene gate, and costs a full verification cycle to diagnose and move — the same class of wasted cycle the proof-hygiene work was created to eliminate. The safe recipe in `docs/tasks/_PROOF_RULE.md` works only when the one easy-to-forget flag is present.

## Fix
Make the capture script default to a task-folder-aware output path so the no-flag invocation is already correct: when `--out` is omitted, resolve the current task id (in order: an explicit env var such as `TASK_ID`/`KAINBAIN_TASK_ID` if the runner sets one, else the `kb/<task-id>` git branch name, else fail with a message naming the expected `--out` form) and write to `docs/tasks/<task-id>/screenshot-<timestamp>.png`, creating the directory as today. Keep an explicit `--out` as an override that always wins. Update the header usage comment, the `_PROOF_RULE.md` recipe, and `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` if they show the default. Add unit tests mirroring the existing `tests/capture-screenshot.test.mjs` style: default resolves into the task folder when the id is discoverable; explicit `--out` wins; no discoverable id fails fast naming `--out`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Running the capture script without `--out` on a task branch writes a valid PNG (magic `89504e47`) under `docs/tasks/<task-id>/`, never repo root.
- [ ] An explicit `--out` still overrides the default exactly as today.
- [ ] With no discoverable task id, the script exits non-zero with a message showing the `--out` form.
- [ ] `npm run check:proof-hygiene`, `npm run check:binaries`, and the existing capture/guard test suites stay green.

## Non-goals
No change to the PNG byte-writing mechanism, the binary guard, or the proof-hygiene detector semantics; no new runtime dependencies.

Follow-on from KainBain task ef569a1a-d301-4e10-aaba-8cde942b97e8 ("Prevent binary proof PNG corruption instead of only detecting it"): its deep review (`docs/tasks/ef569a1a-d301-4e10-aaba-8c

# Default screenshot capture output to the task docs folder

## Problem
The repo's screenshot tool (`scripts/capture-screenshot.mjs`) writes PNG bytes directly, which is the binary-safe way for agents to attach proof screenshots. But its `--out` flag defaults to `screenshot.png` in the repo root (code: `getArg("--out") || "screenshot.png"`). Every agent must therefore remember to pass an explicit `--out docs/tasks/<task-id>/<name>-proof.png` on every capture. If an agent forgets or improvises, the PNG lands at the repo root, trips the repo-root scratch-hygiene gate, and costs a full verification cycle to diagnose and move — the same class of wasted cycle the proof-hygiene work was created to eliminate. The safe recipe in `docs/tasks/_PROOF_RULE.md` works only when the one easy-to-forget flag is present.

## Fix
Make the capture script default to a task-folder-aware output path so the no-flag invocation is already correct: when `--out` is omitted, resolve the current task id (in order: an explicit env var such as `TASK_ID`/`KAINBAIN_TASK_ID` if the runner sets one, else the `kb/<task-id>` git branch name, else fail with a message naming the expected `--out` form) and write to `docs/tasks/<task-id>/screenshot-<timestamp>.png`, creating the directory as today. Keep an explicit `--out` as an override that always wins. Update the header usage comment, the `_PROOF_RULE.md` recipe, and `docs/agent-docs/GitGuidance.md` if they show the default. Add unit tests mirroring the existing `tests/capture-screenshot.test.mjs` style: default resolves into the task folder when the id is discoverable; explicit `--out` wins; no discoverable id fails fast naming `--out`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Running the capture script without `--out` on a task branch writes a valid PNG (magic `89504e47`) under `docs/tasks/<task-id>/`, never repo root.
- [ ] An explicit `--out` still overrides the default exactly as today.
- [ ] With no discoverable task id, the script exits non-zero with a message showing the `--out` form.
- [ ] `npm run check:proof-hygiene`, `npm run check:binaries`, and the existing capture/guard test suites stay green.

## Non-goals
No change to the PNG byte-writing mechanism, the binary guard, or the proof-hygiene detector semantics; no new runtime dependencies.
